name: Der Marner
credit: Der Marner, miniature in the Codex Manesse (Heidelberg, Cod. Pal. germ. 848), c. 1300–1340 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Der Marner was a travelling Swabian poet of the mid-thirteenth century who wrote in Latin and German and composed love songs, riddles and didactic verse.
Two of his songs appear here in Frank C. Nicholson’s translation, Old German Love Songs (1907), made from the minnesingers of the twelfth to fourteenth centuries.

poems.title: Riddle
poems.author: Der Marner
poems.text:
I note a strange thing in all lands:
Yellow and green its hue doth shine;
It has not feet nor eyes nor hands,
Yet lives 'mong men and may incline
Either with rich or poor to dwell.
It binds men oft, though not with bands:
It sails the Danube and the Rhine;
Lordly raiment it commands,
And with princes drinketh wine.
It slinks where ladies are, as well.
It dieth here and waxeth there; it stirs unceasingly
To the first maiden did it slink upon a tree.
The fourth part of the world it slew,
And still doth slay
Fools every day,
A steer sans horn.
It hath reft mortals not a few
Of bliss, life, soul, and made them mourn—
What is this creature, can you tell?

poems.title: The Minstrel
poems.author: Der Marner
